task:
You answer questions about 3GPP RAN4 standardization records using only a dense retrieval tool over the RAN4 record chunks (meeting-report decision chunks, CR chunks and contribution chunks, each printed with its metadata). The tool embeds your query text and prints the nearest chunks by similarity. Run the tool from the repository root with Bash:
  python3 scripts/publication/paper/ongoing/sigir-2027-research/search_records_dense.py --wg RAN4 --query "<withheld sha256=e4ba216b53e675d3ce45a8584de79ecc013718ef83ebd53f29d47d97af594386 chars=4>" [--top N] [--chars N] [--collection NAME]
--query is the text to embed; --top sets how many chunks are printed; --collection restricts the search to one collection named in the output; --chars 0 prints whole chunks. You may search as many times as you need and follow any identifier you read. Do not open any other file, database, graph or service. Answer with a JSON object {"rows": [[...], ...]}. Each row lists the requested fields in this order: <the item's fields>. Use document numbers, meeting names and clause numbers exactly as written in the records (for example R4-2205027, RAN4#102-e, RP-221234, RAN#96, 6.2.1). Disposition values are lower-case codes such as agreed, revised, noted, endorsed, withdrawn, not_pursued. If the records hold no such row, answer {"rows": []}.

items.question: TSG RAN CR pack RP-211890 carries change requests from RAN4. Take each change request in the pack that has a source-verified RAN4 disposition for the whole document and each clause it modifies in the release that change request targets (Rel-16 or Rel-17). For each such clause, look at the change requests of that release that modify the same clause and give every CR pack of the latest earlier TSG RAN meeting in the records that carried such a change request; leave out clauses with no earlier pack. Give the specification, the clause, the CR pack document number, and the TSG RAN meeting.
